You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: Calling Flush on the ETag response writer sends buffered bytes to the client before the response is complete, so the ETag can no longer be set (the request says Flush must not bypass the buffer).

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [minor] Quote-aware split is swallowed by a stray quote, reproduced: `go test -run TestRTQuoteAware` gave 200 for `If-None-Match: "abc, "x"` and `abc"d, "x"` and `W/"y", "x`, where `"x"` is a well-formed member that should match. The criterion's own example `abc, "x"` passes. Decide whether "best effort" covers this.
- [minor] Headers set after `WriteHeader` are sent through ETag but dropped by plain net/http. Reproduced on a real server: `WriteHeader(404)` then `Header().Set("X-Late","1")` gave `X-Late="1"`. Criterion 5 says headers "as the handler wrote them".
- [minor] `Use(Compress(5), ETag)` gives identity and gzip the same strong ETag, `"71a0f557930807ed9117f87f5b59e7ea"` for both. RFC 9110 requires strong validators to differ per content coding. `ETag(Compress(5)(h))` gives distinct values.
- [minor] `Use(NoCache, ETag)` deletes If-None-Match, so a matching request gets 200, not 304. This is NoCache's design, but it is undocumented.
- [minor] The doc says non-200 responses "pass through unchanged". In code they are buffered in full, like 200s, until the handler returns (read in code, not run). The doc also doesn't mention the 128-bit truncation of the hash.
- [minor] `WriteHeader(42)` doesn't panic at the call; the handler keeps running and net/http's "invalid WriteHeader code" panic fires later in `finish` (reproduced).
=== IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 1 (sent after review 1) ===
GOAL: Fix round 1 on the new `middleware.ETag` in go-chi/chi (repo /tmp/ff-eval-idldo04y/workspace). Fix late headers after WriteHeader, and make three doc-comment fixes.

FILES: middleware/etag.go, middleware/etag_test.go (both already written and passing; read them first). Sibling: middleware/compress.go.

CONSTRAINTS: Change only those two files. Keep behavior otherwise identical. Stdlib only.

FIXES:
1. Late headers (code): with plain net/http, header changes made after the final WriteHeader don't reach the wire. Through ETag they do (reproduced: WriteHeader(404), then Header().Set("X-Late","1"), and the client sees X-Late). Fix: when the final status (non-1xx, or 101) is first recorded in WriteHeader, snapshot the headers (Header().Clone()). In finish/send, before the middleware's own ETag/304 changes, make the underlying header map equal that snapshot (delete keys not in it, set the rest). When the handler never called WriteHeader or Write (status set only in finish/Flush), use the headers as they stand. Keep it small. Add tests on a real httptest server: WriteHeader(200), then Header().Set("X-Late","1"), then Write gives no X-Late on the wire; same for 404. Also check that a handler-set ETag set BEFORE WriteHeader is still used for matching.
2. Doc comment on ETag: say that non-200 GET/HEAD responses are buffered too and sent unchanged once the handler returns (not streamed). Say the generated ETag is the first 128 bits of the SHA-256 of the body, hex-encoded and quoted. Add an ordering note: for distinct ETags per content coding, put ETag before Compress, e.g. `r.Use(middleware.ETag, middleware.Compress(5))`, so the hash covers the encoded body. Note that NoCache deletes If-None-Match, so ETag produces no 304s behind it.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: see /tmp/claude-0/-tmp-ff-eval-idldo04y-workspace/6851e853-3a0e-476b-8ed4-6001fbdf17f2/scratchpad/criteria.md. All of them must still hold. Criterion 5 says non-200 headers go out "as the handler wrote them", which is what fix 1 enforces.

CHECKS: `go test -race -run ETag ./middleware`, then at the end `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `test -z "$(gofmt -l .)"`.
